purpose: Frozen hand-label set for measuring classifier/label tier agreement (docs/deferred-work.md item 110, registered prediction 70-85%).

labelAnchor.rule: The tier DEFINITION block of CLASSIFIER_SYSTEM_PROMPT only: simple <=2 files/<=10 iters, medium 3-8 files/10-25 iters, complex 9+ files/25+ iters, and 'Tier accounts for the LARGER of edit scope and investigation scope'.
deliberatelyExcluded: signal words that raise tier by one (stale/outdated/refactor/Phase X/recent change)
labelAnchor.whyExcluded: Labelling with the heuristics would measure whether the classifier obeys its own instructions - near-tautological. Anchoring to the scope rule alone makes each disagreement attributable to a named excluded heuristic, or unexplained.
labelAnchor.statedConstraint: These labels were frozen by a reader who had already read the classifier's system prompt. Anchoring to the scope rule narrows that but does not remove it. Any agreement figure computed here is between the classifier and a scope judgement made by a reader of its own prompt. It CANNOT be reported as agreement with a naive human label.

labellingProcedure.order: The `index` field is the labelling order. Each task was labelled from its own text before the next was read.
labellingProcedure.noRevision: No label was revised after assignment. Any exception must be named in the report with its reason.
labellingProcedure.sourceAIsolation: Source A task strings were extracted with the adjacent `expected:` archetype STRIPPED, so the archetype label sitting next to them in the corpus file could not steer the tier.
labellingProcedure.sourcesLocked: The three sources are fixed. A shortfall is reported as a shortfall; no source is substituted mid-measurement.

A.selectionRule: Every other entry (1-based odd indices 1,3,...,39), deterministic, spanning all archetype groups since the corpus is archetype-ordered. Not cherry-picked.
A.knownBias: These were authored to exercise this classifier, making them the least neutral source. May be easier (designed to be classifiable) or harder (designed to probe edges) - the report states which the observed pattern suggests rather than picking in advance.

B.what: Verbatim task spans from this arc's on-disk plan files and this session's user-issued briefs
B.note: Plan-file entries are commit-level headings with the 'Commit N - ' prefix stripped; that normalization is the only edit.

C.what: Verbatim commit subjects, git log --format=%s, the 10 most recent at frozen HEAD
C.registerCaveat: A commit subject describes work already done, after the fact; a task is a request issued before it. If disagreements cluster here the finding is about register, not the classifier's judgement - to be checked specifically before attributing.

distributionCaveat: The label set is skewed toward simple (27/40), a property of the material: the corpus carries many listing/question tasks and Source C carries many single-file docs commits. A sparse complex row makes the confusion matrix weak in that cell, and agreement could be inflated if the classifier also defaults toward one tier. Reported, not corrected for.
